## Course anchors

- [With Great Powers: A Practical Guide to Agentic AI for Social Science Research](https://simonepaciphd.github.io/with-great-powers/): researcher control and radical transparency.
- [Working with AI Agents](https://simonepaciphd.github.io/ai-os-public/): the instructor's public guide and research-workspace practices.
- [AI OS public repository](https://github.com/simonepaciphd/ai-os-public): public operating-system materials.

## Foundations

These primary sources anchor specific concepts in the foundation draft. They are background references, rather than a requirement to read every paper in full.

- Vaswani et al. (2017), [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762): transformers and attention.
- Brown et al. (2020), [Language Models are Few-Shot Learners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165): conditioning on examples without gradient updates.
- Ouyang et al. (2022), [Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155): one post-training pathway and its limits.
- Penedo et al. (2024), [The FineWeb Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17557): an example of training-data preparation.
- Lin, Hilton, and Evans (2021), [TruthfulQA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.07958): a benchmark examining learned human falsehoods.

## Workflows and societal governance

- [Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents), Anthropic: design patterns for workflows and agent systems. The article is a historical design reference, not current installation instructions.
- [International AI Safety Report 2026](https://internationalaisafetyreport.org/publication/international-ai-safety-report-2026): candidate risk and uncertainty excerpts.
- [Stanford AI Index 2026](https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report): candidate societal evidence.
- [Governing with Artificial Intelligence](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2025/06/governing-with-artificial-intelligence_398fa287.html), OECD (2025): candidate public-sector governance material.

Final excerpts and discussion readings remain under review. The reports cover different questions and should not be treated as a single agreed account of AI's effects.
